cards.explanation: The answer is False. David says, "In God alone my soul finds rest…" There's no "and my own strength" tacked on the end, friends. His rest comes from God, and so does his salvation. I tried resting on my own strength once, and I'm telling you, my mustache gave out before I did.

The answer is that he will never be shaken. David says, "He alone is my rock and my salvation. He is my fortress; I will never be shaken." Rock and fortress are about as sturdy as it gets. David's standing there like a pan that never warps, and I'm proud of him, friends.

The answer is that they intend to cast him down from his lofty perch. David says, "They fully intend to cast him down from his lofty perch…" Fully intend! They didn't wander into it, they came with a whole plan. And still David tells his soul to rest in God (Psalm 62:5).

The answer is curse. David says, "with their mouths they bless, but inwardly they curse." Smiling on the outside, cursing on the inside. That's like a cookie box with a pretty bow and nothing but crumbs rattling around in there, friends.

The answer is that his hope comes from Him. David says, "Rest in God alone, O my soul, for my hope comes from Him." His hope has one source, and he's talking to his own soul about it. I do that too, friends, mostly when the dough won't cooperate.

The answer is True. David says, "Trust in Him at all times, O people; pour out your hearts before Him." He's been talking to his own soul, and now he turns to everyone else. Pouring out your heart before God means holding nothing back, and I think that sounds like a relief, friends.

The answer is that they weigh next to nothing. David says, "Weighed on the scale, they go up; together they are but a vapor." When the scale goes up, there's hardly anything on it. Picture a scale with a puff of steam on it, and it just bobs there like it's embarrassed.

The answer is False. David says, "If your riches increase, do not set your heart upon them." Just before that he says, "Place no trust in extortion or false hope in stolen goods." Money can come in, friends, but your heart shouldn't move in with it.

The answer is that power belongs to God. David says, "God has spoken once; I have heard this twice: that power belongs to God…" Whatever else is loud in the world, friends, the power is God's. That's the line to hold onto.

The answer is deeds. David says, "For You will repay each man according to his deeds." Not by bank account, not by family name. It's what a person has done. That's how David closes the psalm, friends.
